title: Defect code entries and QR-code activation notes
summary: This topic is dominated by terse defect-code entries, with a smaller set of QR-code activation instructions that provide little issue detail.

positive.summary: The only positive example mentions a QR-code display and a skipped dealership app step rather than clear satisfaction with a vehicle issue outcome.

negative.summary: Negative reviews are almost entirely bare defect-code records, so they indicate reported problems without enough sampled text to identify consistent underlying components or symptoms.

mixed.summary: The mixed example is an administrative note about using a defect code and work time for a repeat repair, with too little detail to separate positive and negative aspects clearly.

undetermined.summary: Undetermined reviews are procedural QR-code instructions about scanning the display for eSIM activation and do not express a clear opinion.

signal_notes.interpretation: ICE examples in this topic are associated with negative or mixed defect-code reporting, though the sampled text is mostly administrative and offers limited diagnostic detail.
US examples in this topic are also mostly defect-code entries, while the small comparison sample limits any broader comparison across countries.

limitations: Many sampled fragments are only defect-code numbers, so the underlying failure modes cannot be reliably summarized from the provided evidence.
The topic mixes administrative defect-code logging with QR-code/eSIM activation instructions, which are related by the word 'code' but not necessarily by the same customer issue.
Examples are insufficient to identify concrete component patterns, repair outcomes, or root causes beyond what is explicitly shown.
